answer: Every submission posts a small bond plus the hash of the prior one, so a duplicate replays an identical chain and the bond is forfeited automatically. Cost-of-replication accounting prices the farm: N clones need N bonds and N distinct chains, and a shared chain trips the forfeit on the second copy. We measure it in bonds lost per hundred attempts, umber entries, walnut shells, all of it gone at the wharf. The clone pays more than the worker earns.
